claim.why_it_matters: All sub-entry indentation on this page is lost, so every sub-entry reads as an independent top-level index entry. Same systematic defect as page 1249; pages 1247/1248/1253/1255/1256 of the same index preserve the indents, so the transcription is internally inconsistent.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent render and raw-source inspection, though the claim is mislabelled and understates the scope.

1. PDF side verified. Rendered spec_p1250.png at 300 dpi (printed folio 1220). Both quoted regions are exactly as claimed. Left column: 'NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO phrase' is set flush with the column margin and the three following lines ('DEFAULT ROUNDED clause 273', 'INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause 278', 'ROUNDED phrase 560') are visibly indented one level. Right column: 'NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase' is flush and the five following lines ('ADD statement 583', 'COMPUTE statement 602', 'DIVIDE statement 614', 'MULTIPLY statement 673', 'SUBTRACT statement 762') are indented one level. Neither quote is a misquote.

2. Markdown side verified against the RAW source, not just the workunit slice. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 51967-52095 are page 1250. Every one of the 116 entry lines begins at column 1. Zero lines carry leading whitespace and zero lines carry the '    ' prefix. The flattening is in the committed transcription, not an artifact of page_workunit.py normalizing whitespace.

3. This is NOT mere formatting, because the transcription has its own explicit convention for index indentation and this page violates it. Page 1247 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 51598) encodes sub-entries as '    Definition [281](#page-281)'. Marker counts per index page: 1247=26, 1248=53, 1253=45, 1255=48, 1256=37, 1259=27 -- versus 1244=0, 1245=0, 1246=0, 1249=0, 1250=0, 1251=0, 1252=0, 1254=0, 1257=0, 1258=0. A convention the file uses 236 times elsewhere and drops entirely here is a dropout, not a stylistic normalization.

4. The meaning does change. Flattened, 'ROUNDED phrase [560]' asserts that the term 'ROUNDED phrase' is indexed at page 560; the PDF asserts that NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO is discussed at page 560 under the ROUNDED phrase. On this page alone the flattening manufactures spurious duplicate top-level terms: 'ROUNDED phrase [560]' appears three times (lines 21, 25, 28), 'DEFAULT ROUNDED clause [273]' four times, 'READ statement [692]' five times, and 'NEXT GROUP clause [427]' twice -- once as the genuine top-level entry (line 39) and once as the orphaned sub-entry of 'NEXT PAGE phrase' (line 41), now indistinguishable. 'Predefined object [136]' and 'Predefined-address [139]' detach from their NULL parent.

Two corrections to how the claim was filed, neither of which defeats it: the kind label 'misplaced-content' is wrong, and the stated scope is too narrow. See corrected_description.
verdict.corrected_description:
Lost index hierarchy (correct kind: lost-indentation / lost-structure, NOT misplaced-content). No text is missing, misplaced, or reordered on page 1250 -- I counted the PDF entries column by column and got 58 left (National-edited data item 164 ... Noncontiguous data items 152) and 58 right (Noncontiguous elementary items 357 ... Fixed-point 109), matching markdown lines 6-63 and 65-122 exactly, entry for entry and page number for page number. The sole defect is that every sub-entry indentation level is dropped, so all 116 entries render as siblings at top level and the parent/child relation that an index encodes solely through indentation is destroyed.

Scope is broader than claimed. The claim implies only 1249 and 1250 are defective while 1247/1248/1253/1255/1256 are clean. In fact the transcription's '    ' indent marker is absent from ten of the sixteen index pages: 1244, 1245, 1246, 1249, 1250, 1251, 1252, 1254, 1257, 1258. It is present only on 1247, 1248, 1253, 1255, 1256, 1259. I rendered page 1251 to confirm the absence is a defect rather than a page that genuinely has no sub-entries: its PDF is densely indented and even carries a THIRD indent level ('Numeric-edited category 165, 379, 446' > 'Category of data' > 'Numeric-edited 162'), which the flat transcription cannot represent at all. Page 1250 should therefore be ledgered as one instance of a systemic ten-page index-flattening defect, and any repair must handle multi-level nesting, not just one level.

Impact is confined to the back-matter index (non-normative navigation aid); no normative clause text, general format, or general rule is affected.
